title: Toyota Motor Corporation | Business and Management - EBSCO
content: Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi, Japan, is a leading global automobile manufacturer known for its diverse range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and hybrids. It became the world's largest automaker in 2008 and remains a significant player in the automotive industry, employing over 370,000 individuals and producing more than 200 million vehicles since its inception. Toyota is recognized for pioneering the hybrid vehicle market with the introduction of the Prius in 1997, which was the first mass-produced hybrid automobile. Toyota's impact extends beyond manufacturing; it plays a significant role in the global economy and has strategic partnerships, such as its collaboration with Mazda.
